# `sesam init --recipient` stores the spec instead of the raw key, so the admin's
# key source lands in sesam.yml and the audit log. file:// stands in for forge
# specs, which need a live forge.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

mkdir keys
exec sh -c 'echo "$ADMIN_PUBKEY" > keys/admin.pub'
exec sh -c 'echo "$BOB_PUBKEY" > keys/bob.pub'
exec sh -c 'printf "%s\n%s\n" "$BOB_PUBKEY" "$ADMIN_PUBKEY" > keys/both.pub'

# A spec that does not match the identity is refused and leaves nothing behind.
! exec sesam init --user admin --recipient file://keys/bob.pub
stderr 'do not include identity key'
stderr $ADMIN_PUBKEY
! exists .sesam
! exists sesam.yml

# Unresolvable specs fail before anything is written.
! exec sesam init --user admin --recipient file://keys/missing.pub
! exists .sesam

# Like a forge account with several devices: the spec resolves to more keys
# than the identity holds. The extra ones are kept as admin recipients.
exec sesam init --user admin --recipient file://keys/both.pub
grep 'file://keys/both.pub' sesam.yml
! grep 'age1' sesam.yml
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout 'file://keys/both.pub'
stdout $ADMIN_PUBKEY
stdout $BOB_PUBKEY

exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'
exec sesam verify
